name: Luna 2
note: First human-made object to reach the Moon.

name: Ranger 7
note: Sent back close-up photos until impact.

name: Luna 9
note: First soft landing and first photos from the surface. LRO hasn't found the lander; the true site is likely within about 10 km.

name: Surveyor 1
note: First US soft landing.

name: Surveyor 3
note: Apollo 12 landed within walking distance and brought pieces of it home.

name: Surveyor 4
note: Contact lost minutes before touchdown.

name: Surveyor 6
note: First spacecraft to lift off from the Moon, hopping a few meters.

name: Apollo 11
note: First humans on the Moon.

name: Luna 15
note: Crashed while Apollo 11's astronauts were still on the surface.

name: Luna 16
note: First robotic sample return.

name: Luna 17
note: Delivered Lunokhod 1, the first rover on another world.

name: Apollo 17
note: The last time people walked on the Moon.

name: Luna 23
partial: Damaged on landing; it couldn't collect its sample.

name: Lunar Prospector
note: Steered into a polar crater to look for water.

name: LCROSS
note: Its rocket stage hit a permanently shadowed crater and the spacecraft flew through the plume, which contained water.

name: GRAIL A and B
note: Twin gravity-mapping spacecraft, crashed side by side on purpose.

name: Chang'e 3
note: First soft landing in 37 years.

name: LADEE
site: Near Sundman V crater, far side

name: Chang'e 4
note: First landing on the far side.

name: Beresheet
note: First privately funded spacecraft to reach the Moon.

name: Luna 25
note: Russia's first lunar mission since 1976.

name: Chandrayaan-3
note: First soft landing this close to the south pole.

name: SLIM
partial: Landed on its nose after losing an engine, but within about 100 m of its target.

name: Odysseus (IM-1)
site: Malapert A crater, near the south pole
partial: Caught a leg and tipped onto its side, but kept working.
note: First commercial soft landing, and the first US landing since 1972.

name: Chang'e 6
note: First samples from the far side.

name: Blue Ghost Mission 1
note: First fully successful commercial landing.

name: Athena (IM-2)
site: Mons Mouton, near the south pole
partial: Landed on its side in a crater and shut down early.
